title: Phase 1 One Pool Worker Runtime
description:
Phase 1 of the Interactive Job Runtime Refactor (master ticket 26/08/20/INTERACTIVE-JOB-RUNTIME-REFACTOR).

Replace all role-specific thread allocation with ONE process-wide worker pool executing logical lanes.

Targets:
- cpu_worker_count = max(1, N-1) for interactive native processes (UI thread reserved); N for headless batch. On wasm32 the pool degrades to a cooperative host-driven scheduler.
- Kernel, actor shards, compute, I/O and timers all become logical lanes on the single substrate. No nested or subsystem-owned CPU pools anywhere.
- Checked permit ledger in release builds: over-allocation returns an error and never wraps. Replaces ThreadBudget, whose checkout currently wraps silently in release (debug_assert only).
- Worker admission control: background lanes may not occupy all workers while a UI is live; at least one slot stays available to interactive and preview work when there are 2+ workers.
- run_blocking removed from the interactive host runtime trait; block_on restricted to approved process and test entry points.
- Structured scopes, cancellation and ChannelPolicy retained, with channel capacities extended to cover both item counts and bytes.

Phase 0 census established the real scope: 28 thread-creation sites; 15 deterministic threads on a 10-core native session plus unbounded ad-hoc threads. Five sites need genuine restructuring rather than a call-site swap: ShardExecutor (5 ms poll loop), shard outcome forwarders (250 ms poll loop), per-actor DB threads, the store-sync actor (per-document thread plus an embedded tokio runtime), and the epoch ticker (1 ms poll loop).

Exit gate: a thread census shows exactly the UI thread plus pool workers; no subsystem can create a CPU pool; permit over-allocation errors in release; the interactivity audit's thread-pool findings drop to the sanctioned runtime module only.
